title: Christmas lights war with my neighbor
author: Storytime
hook: For five years, my neighbor and I have had a Christmas lights war. This year, his lights spelled out a message. For me.
story: It started five years ago, the winter after my husband passed. I put up a few lights, just to feel normal. The next day, my neighbor Frank put up twice as many. So I bought more. So did he. By year three, we each had a reindeer on the roof. Last year, people drove in from other towns to see our street. Frank and I barely spoke the rest of the year. Just a nod over the fence. And every December, a little note in my mailbox. Your move. Last night, he turned his lights on for the season. His entire roof was covered in white bulbs. They spelled four words. Coffee, Sunday? Your move. My granddaughter was screaming. Then his son came over and told me something. Frank's wife passed the same year as my husband. He started the lights war because it was the only way he knew how to talk to me. He's been trying to ask me for coffee for five years. He's seventy-four. I'm seventy-two. My whole family says I should say yes. How should I answer him? With lights?
caption: five years of lights just to ask me for coffee 🎄 #storytime
sound: a soft, cozy Christmas jazz piano at very low volume
why: Holiday light feuds between neighbors are trending, the your move notes are the planted clue, the rivalry-to-romance twist is shareable, and answer with lights invites creative comments.

title: Sister sold the plane ticket I bought her
author: Storytime
hook: I paid for my sister's flight home for Thanksgiving. She sold the ticket. Then I found out who she sold it for.
story: My sister Ava lives across the country and money's been tight for her. So in September, I bought her a plane ticket home for Thanksgiving. Four hundred dollars. Mom was so excited. Last week, Ava called me. She said, please don't be mad, but I sold the ticket. I was mad. Really mad. I asked her what she spent the money on. She said, gas. I didn't understand. Then she sent me a photo. Her, in a beat up car, at a gas station somewhere in Nebraska. And in the passenger seat was our brother, Luke. Luke hasn't been home in six years. After a huge fight with our dad, he just left. He's been working odd jobs, couldn't afford a ticket, and was too proud to ask. Ava sold her flight to pay for a two day road trip, so she could pick him up on the way. Our dad has no idea. Mom has no idea. They're arriving Thursday morning. Ava asked me not to tell anyone, because Luke might turn around if there's pressure. Should I warn my dad, or let it be a surprise?
caption: she sold the ticket for the best reason 🦃 #storytime
sound: an emotional, hopeful road trip guitar at very low volume
why: Thanksgiving travel and family reunions spike now, the sold ticket makes viewers angry first, the brother reveal flips it, and the warn or surprise question splits the comments.

title: Coworker microwaves fish every day
author: Storytime
hook: My coworker microwaves fish in the office every single day. I complained to HR. Then she told me why.
story: Our office kitchen is tiny. And every day at noon, my coworker Denise microwaves salmon. Every single day. The whole floor smells like fish until three. People complain. Denise just smiles and says, sorry, doctor's orders. Last month, I finally reported her to HR. The next morning, Denise asked me to grab coffee. I expected a fight. Instead, she asked me a question. Have you noticed where Mark sits? Mark is our manager. His desk is right next to the kitchen. Then she asked, have you noticed what he does when the new girls get coffee? I had. He hovers. He stands too close. He makes comments. The new intern, Chloe, had started bringing her lunch in a bag and eating in her car. Denise said, Mark hates fish. He leaves his desk the second that microwave starts. Every day at noon, for an hour, Chloe can eat lunch in peace. I felt sick. I'd reported the wrong person. This morning, I went back to HR. Not about the fish. About Mark. Denise is coming with me. Wish us luck?
caption: the fish was a shield 🐟 #storytime
sound: a tense corporate beat that turns empowering at very low volume
why: Office microwave fish is a universally relatable pet peeve, doctor's orders is a misleading clue, the protective twist flips the villain, and wish us luck drives supportive comments.
